Part 1 · Building and fabrication

How do drawings become parts standing in a building?

Six phases, one building, one skid

  1. The construction sequencesix phases, each with its photo
  2. A building for hydrogenventilation, doors, cylinders outside

Part 1 · the construction sequence

Step through the build

Each phase ends with a record that releases the next. Faces and logos are blurred.

Part 1 · a building for hydrogen

The building is part of the safety design

  • H₂ rises: louvres and a high roof let it out.
  • Cylinder packs stand outside, under a shelter.
  • Two roller doors: crane access, second escape.
  • Gas detectors GD-001/002 on the HMI.

Part 1 · fabrication in the workshop

Two items, two kinds of joint

R-601 · GA A3E-602 · CAL R1
Body3" sch 80S TP316L, 4.0 mTEMA BEM, 38 tubes ½"
Jointsbutt welds, GTAWtubes expanded
NDERT full, PT 100 %leak at test
Mass158 kg empty82.66 kg dry

An argon purge keeps the root weld clean where catalyst and H₂ sit.

Part 1 · what R-601 weighs

Rebuild the weight from its parts

Pipe 15.5 kg/m from its dimensions; flange masses are typical catalogue values, assumed.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Six phases, each released by a record.
  • The building ventilates H₂ and keeps cylinders outside.
  • R-601 is welded and radiographed; E-602 tubes are expanded.
  • R-601: 158 kg empty, 176 kg full of water (GA A3).

The weight is the first line of the lift plan.

Part 2 · Lifting into the building

How do you lift a reactor into a building safely?

Part 2 · the plan

Load, chart, height

  1. The loadssix lifts, from documents or estimated
  2. The lift checkgross load against the crane chart at radius
  3. Hook height and boomwhat governs a light, tall load
  4. What the photos showa vertical lift through the platform

Part 2 · the loads

Six lifts with a truck-loader crane

Masses from GA A3 and CAL R1 where they exist; radii, heights and the platform are assumed.

Part 2 · the lift check

Four numbers decide a lift

$W_g=W(1+c)+W_r$contingency on the load, plus slings, shackles and hook block
$u=W_g/C(R)$chart capacity at the working radius
$H_{hook}=H_{land}+h+s+0.5$landing level, load height, slings, clearance
$L=\sqrt{R^2+(H_{hook}+1-H_p)^2}$boom tip 1 m above the hook

W load, kg · c contingency · Wr rigging, kg · R radius, m · h load height · s sling height · Hp boom pivot 2.4 m (assumed).

Part 2 · the lift check

Is the load inside the chart?

Chart: a typical 5 t truck-loader crane, assumed, not the crane on site. Limits ≤ 75 % routine, ≤ 90 % critical (assumed).

Part 2 · hook height and boom

Light load, tall lift: what governs?

R-601 at 6 % of the chart still needs a 9.5 m hook. Roof height is not in the documents: try it.

Part 2 · what the photos show

A vertical lift through the platform

  • Truck crane inside, through the roller door.
  • Load wrapped, lifted by its lugs.
  • Riggers on the platform clipped on.
  • Area below barricaded.

Each of these is a control written into the job safety analysis.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Gross load = load × (1 + contingency) + rigging.
  • Every lift here is below 30 % of the assumed chart.
  • R-601 needs a 9.5 m hook and an 8.8 m boom.
  • Roof height and floor capacity are not in the documents.

Part 3 · Safe work and completion

When is the unit mechanically complete?

Part 3 · the plan

Hazards, punch list, certificate

  1. Job safety analysisthe R-601 lift, step by step
  2. Mechanical completionwhat the certificate means
  3. Punch list A or Bwhat must close before fluids go in
  4. The completion checklistwhen the certificate can be signed

Part 3 · job safety analysis

Lifting R-601 into the skid, step by step

Each step names its hazard and its control; the permit to work points to this JSA.

Part 3 · mechanical completion

Built as designed, and tested

  • Strength and leak tests passed.
  • Walk-down against the P&ID done.
  • Every punch A item closed.
  • B items open with owner and date.

The certificate hands the unit to pre-commissioning.

Part 3 · punch list

Sort each open item: A or B?

A blocks safe pressurising or fluids in; B can close after start-up. Items are examples, assumed.

Part 3 · the completion checklist

Can the certificate be signed?

One unticked line keeps the certificate unsigned: completion is all or nothing.

Part 3 · checks

What the documents still have to settle

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • The JSA ties each lift step to a hazard and a control.
  • Work at height: harness clipped on, every time.
  • A items close before fluids; B items after start-up.
  • Completion is signed only when every line is ticked.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

The building is part of the H₂ safety design.

2

Weights come from documents; check them by rebuilding.

3

For light, tall loads, hook height governs the lift.

4

Every lift step has a hazard and a named control.

5

Close punch A before any pressure or fluid.
